quotes.text: The only way out is to stop treating PBIX as a sacred artifact and start thinking of your model as code. That mental shift means better history, cleaner teamwork, and fewer nights spent piecing together ten mismatched final files.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the central mindset shift of the episode.

quotes.text: Treating models like code doesn't mean learning c paws at midnight. It just means the things you're already doing, editing docks, adding relationships, adjusting tables, get locked in a structured format.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Addresses the common objection that BI people don't code.

quotes.text: You build in development, validate in tests, then promote into production. It's moving from wild west published directly to controlled stage by stage promotion.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concise description of the Dev-Test-Prod principle.

quotes.text: At minimum, snapshot your production data set and tag the corresponding Git commit before you publish. That gives you a rollback point.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical mitigation step teams can apply immediately.

quotes.text: Fixing a metric without documenting the reason is like patching a leaky pipe and throwing away the blueprint.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable argument for linking changes to tickets.

chapters.title: Treating Power BI models like real code
Git, the secret weapon for BI teams

takeaways: Extract Power BI models from binary PBIX files into text so Git can show meaningful diffs and history.
Use Dev, Test and Prod stages in deployment pipelines so changes are validated before they reach end users.
Link every commit and promotion to a ticket so the business reason behind each change stays traceable.
hook: Emailing PBIX files and publishing straight to production turns Power BI work into firefighting. This episode shows BI teams how to treat models as code, use Git and Dev-Test-Prod deployment pipelines, and tie changes to tickets for governed, reliable releases.
